classification.classification_note: The observed fault is a heap over-read: `userDataDecoder()` dispatches `NikonTagsDecoder()` with only 24 declared `NCTG` payload bytes, `NikonTagsDecoder()` ignores that bound, accepts `dataLength == 200` into `DataBuf buf(200)` without spare space for a terminator, and later passes the non-terminated buffer to `strlen` through `Exiv2::toString(unsigned char*)`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42530135 (exiv2): Heap-buffer-overflow READ {*} found by fuzz target fuzz-read-print-write [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42530135
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source / staged poc
bug_description.normalized: The staged 248-byte witness (sha256 `cf5f4b60c899daeaaa5766b82c1c4d906aeef2e95a276c92ea03873af76312b2`) is a BMFF/QuickTime file whose case-insensitive `Udta` box begins at offset `0x18` with header `00 00 00 4b 55 64 74 61`. Inside it, offsets `0x20..0x27` are `00 00 00 20 4e 43 54 47`, so `userDataDecoder()` declares an `NCTG` child atom of total size 32 and calls `NikonTagsDecoder(size - 8)` with only 24 declared payload bytes. `NikonTagsDecoder()` then allocates `DataBuf buf(200)` and iterates `for (int i = 0; i < 100; i++)` without decrementing or checking `size_external`; the parameter is only used by the final rewind at line 1052. On the first record, offsets `0x28..0x2f` are `00 00 00 16 00 02 00 c8`, which decode to `TagID 0x0016` (`Xmp.video.FrameRate`), `dataType 0x0002`, and `dataLength 200`. After `std::memset()` zeroes the 200-byte buffer, the guard `if (dataLength > 200)` still accepts this exact-fit case and `io_->readOrThrow(buf.data(), dataLength)` reads 200 bytes starting at `0x30`: only the first 16 bytes are still within the declared `NCTG` payload, and the remaining 184 bytes come from subsequent file data through `0xf7`. That 200-byte span contains no `0x00`, so `xmpData_[...] = Exiv2::toString(buf.data())` passes a non-terminated `unsigned char*` to `Exiv2::toString`, `os << arg` reaches `strlen`, and Stage 01 reproduces `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 201` at the byte immediately past the 200-byte allocation. The fix makes the buffer 201 bytes, rejects `dataLength >= buf.size()`, and appends `buf.data()[dataLength] = '\0'`.

source.description: First project-side parse on the vulnerable path that materializes the declared size of the attacker-controlled `NCTG` child atom.
source.value_from: The staged 248-byte `poc` has sha256 `cf5f4b60c899daeaaa5766b82c1c4d906aeef2e95a276c92ea03873af76312b2`. At offsets `0x20..0x23`, bytes `00 00 00 20` decode here to `size == 32`, which later becomes `size_external == 24` in `NikonTagsDecoder(size - 8)`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The only guard rejects values strictly larger than the 200-byte heap buffer, so the exact-fit `dataLength == 200` case is accepted even though the later C-string conversion still needs one extra byte for `\0`.
root_cause.note: The staged fix changes the allocation to `DataBuf buf(201)`, tightens this guard to `if (dataLength >= buf.size())`, and writes `buf.data()[dataLength] = '\0'` after the read.

sink.description: Project sink that forwards the non-terminated Nikon payload pointer into the stream insertion path for `unsigned char*`, causing `strlen` to scan past the 200-byte heap allocation.
sink.note: The saved ASan stack is `strlen -> length -> operator<< -> Exiv2::toString<unsigned char*> -> QuickTimeVideo::NikonTagsDecoder`, so this line is the immediate project call site of the crashing `strlen` frame.

tainted_value_origin.description: This read materializes the attacker-controlled Nikon text length that drives the exact-fit guard and the subsequent 200-byte payload read.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: At offsets `0x2e..0x2f` of the staged `poc`, bytes `00 c8` decode here to `dataLength == 200` for the first Nikon tag record, even though the whole declared `NCTG` payload is only 24 bytes.

parser_admitted.description: Within the case-insensitive `Udta` parser, child header bytes `00 00 00 20 4e 43 54 47` cause `userDataDecoder()` to dispatch the `NCTG` child to `NikonTagsDecoder()` with `size_external == 24`.

fine_trace.note: Source. Inside the staged `Udta` payload, bytes `00 00 00 20` at offsets `0x20..0x23` decode to `size == 32` for the next child atom. That declared size later becomes `size_external == 24` when the child is dispatched to `NikonTagsDecoder()`.
The following four bytes are `4e 43 54 47` (`NCTG`), so `userDataDecoder()` dispatches the child to `NikonTagsDecoder()` with only `size - 8 == 24` declared payload bytes.

Destination extent. The Nikon tag decoder allocates a 200-byte heap buffer for generic text values. The saved ASan allocation stack points to this constructor and later reports the over-read at the first byte past this 200-byte region.

Entered with `size_external == 24`, the decoder starts a fixed 100-iteration record loop. The loop body never decrements or checks `size_external`; the parameter is only used by the cleanup seek at line 1052 after the loop, so the first record can read past the declared `NCTG` payload before any rewind happens.

The first record header bytes at `0x28..0x2b` decode to `TagID == 0x0016`. `find(NikonNCTGTags, TagID)` resolves this entry to `Xmp.video.FrameRate`, so the later `if (td)` gate can publish the value through the generic string path.
The next two bytes `00 02` set `dataType == 2`, selecting the text-value decoder rather than the numeric arms.
After zeroing `buf`, the decoder reads the record length field into `buf[0..1]`. The staged bytes at offsets `0x2e..0x2f` are `00 c8`, and they are still inside the declared 24-byte `NCTG` payload.

fine_trace.code:
else if (dataType == 2 || dataType == 7) {
  dataLength = buf.read_uint16(0, bigEndian);
fine_trace.note: Because `TagID` was not one of the two Nikon special cases and `dataType == 2`, the generic string arm interprets those two bytes as `dataLength == 200`. This value later controls both the size guard and the payload read size.

Root-cause step. The only size check rejects values strictly larger than the 200-byte allocation. The exact-fit case `dataLength == 200` is accepted even though the later C-string conversion still needs one extra byte for `\0`.

After `std::memset(buf.data(), 0x0, buf.size())`, this read copies 200 bytes starting at file offset `0x30` into the 200-byte heap buffer. Only the first 16 of those bytes (`0x30..0x3f`) are still within the declared `NCTG` payload; the remaining 184 bytes come from subsequent file data (`0x40..0xf7`). The 200-byte span contains no `0x00`, so the read overwrites the buffer's only in-bounds terminator.
Because step 5 resolved `td` for `TagID 0x0016`, the `if (td)` gate passes and the now non-terminated 200-byte buffer is forwarded to `Exiv2::toString()` as the FrameRate value.

Sink. In `Exiv2::toString<unsigned char*>`, stream insertion treats the same pointer as a C string and reaches `strlen`. With no `\0` inside the 200-byte allocation, ASan reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 201` at the first byte past `buf`.

poc.trigger: Feeding the staged 248-byte BMFF witness to the vulnerable `fuzz-read-print-write` target reproduces the saved `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 201` in `strlen` after `userDataDecoder()` dispatches `NikonTagsDecoder()` with only 24 declared `NCTG` payload bytes, `NikonTagsDecoder()` reads a 200-byte FrameRate value into `buf(200)`, and `Exiv2::toString(buf.data())` scans past the allocation.

format.name: 248-byte BMFF/QuickTime file with a 32-byte `NCTG` atom whose first record claims a 200-byte string
format.contract: The witness begins with `00 00 00 18 66 74 79 70 69 73 6f 6d` and inside a case-insensitive `Udta` box contains child header bytes `00 00 00 20 4e 43 54 47` at offsets `0x20..0x27`, declaring an `NCTG` atom of total size 32 and a payload of only 24 bytes. The first record header at offsets `0x28..0x2f` is `00 00 00 16 00 02 00 c8`, so the vulnerable decoder sees `TagID 0x0016`, `dataType 2`, and `dataLength 200`. Because `NikonTagsDecoder(size - 8)` ignores `size_external == 24` while iterating records, it reads 200 bytes from offset `0x30` into `DataBuf buf(200)` even though only the first 16 bytes of that span are inside the declared `NCTG` payload; those 200 bytes contain no `0x00`. The exact-fit `dataLength > 200` guard lets this through, and `Exiv2::toString(buf.data())` later over-reads the heap buffer.
